question: If the sum of the first \(3n\) positive integers is \(150\) more than the sum of the first \(n\) positive integers, then the sum of the first \(4n\) positive integers is:
solution:
Subtracting the sum of the first \(n\) integers from the sum of the first \(3n\) leaves
\[
(n+1)+(n+2)+\cdots+3n=150,
\]
where \(n\) is a positive integer. Pair the first term with the last, the second with the next-to-last, and so on. Each pair sums to \(4n+1\). There are \(2n\) terms, so all terms form exactly \(n\) pairs.

Now pair the integers from \(1\) through \(4n\) in the same way. Every pair again sums to \(4n+1\), but these \(4n\) terms form \(2n\) pairs. There are twice as many pairs of the same size, so the required sum is
\[
2\cdot150=\boxed{300},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
